Amst-fium pag. 52." beside the lines of paragraph 6, and "Armin. dij." with "16. th.7." beside the lines at the foot of the text. Running head at top left, page number at top right. main_text.p: fuæ hunc indeclinabiliter converteret, non illum, & fic efficacia gratiæ reducenda foret in Dei voluntatem determinantem, non in liberum arbitrium humanum. 4. Hæc ἐυδοκία[?] discriminat non tantum fastuosos ab humilibus, sed & totum genus humanum in duas classes dividit v 27. Neque cognoscit quis Patrem, præter filium, ᾧ ἂν βούληται ὁ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψη[?]. Discriminatio itaque hæc directe refertur, non in voluntates sapientum & parvulorum, sed in Dei voluntatem revelantem patrem, cui vult. 5. Nullo colore Christus gratias agit Patri propter nudum decretum, sed eo quod suis discipulis & parvulis, non principibus hujus mundi dignitate & sapientia præclaris Chri-stum revelaret. 6. Grevinchovius negat hic a-gi de revelatione fideiContr. Amst-fium pag. 52.( nisi ( inquit ) forte fi-dem pro objecto fidei acceperis. Atqui doctrina fidei non tantum parvulis, sed & sapientibus revelata fuit. Alioqui quomodo fieri potuit ut sapientes hanc doctrinam odio & fastidio haberent? non revelata quis odio haberet? Si vero per τὸ[?] revelare hic notent actu fe-cundo illuminare, loquaturtu[?] necesse est hic Salvatorde[?] fidei ingeneratione, & sic humilitas habitualis erit causa efficaciæ hujus revelationis, quod absurdum est. 7. Si sapientes & parvuli sunt objectnm[?] formale hujus decreti, tum ii quibus revelatur hoc mysterium semper erunt indigniores & deteriores hisce, quibus non revelatur. page.notes: Running head and page number read as printed. The catchword "pa-" stands at the foot right and is not repeated in the text. Ee 2 is the gathering signature. Uncertain readings: the first Greek word (ἐυδοκία), the Greek in the passage on revealing (τὸ), "loquaturtu" and "Salvatorde" are run together or unclear in the scan, and "objectnm" may be a printing error for "objectum". The marginal reference "Armin. dij." is read as printed; the abbreviation may be "dis." Greek accents and breathings in the quotation from Scripture are uncertain. Marginal reference "Contr. Amst-fium pag. 52." is read across two lines in the margin.
